title: Reverse Hölder inequality
statement: Let $p\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $p<1$ and $p\ne0$. For all nonnegative real-valued functions $f,g$ on the Boolean cube, $\langle f,g\rangle\ge M_p(f)M_{p/(p-1)}(g)$, where the inner product and extended power means use uniform expectation.
hypotheses_covered: f and g are real-valued functions on the Boolean cube
f is nonnegative at every cube point
g is nonnegative at every cube point
replaced: Let $p<1$, $p\ne0$, and $f,g:\{0,1\}^n\to[0,\infty)$. Then $\E[fg]\ge M_p(f)M_{p/(p-1)}(g)$. For nonnegative functions $u$, the extended mean is $M_r(u)=(\E u^r)^{1/r}$ when $r>0$; the same formula applies for $r<0$ when $u$ is positive everywhere. For positive $u$, $M_0(u)=\exp(\E\log u)$; if $r\le0$ and $u$ has a zero, $M_r(u)=0$. All expectations are uniform.
